articles.headline: Your Stress Hormone Is Secretly Helping You Heal
articles.body: A research team at Max Planck Institute found that the stress hormone CRH actually accelerates brain repair after injury. When brain tissue gets damaged, myelin-producing cells rapidly release CRH to control how those cells mature and rebuild protective nerve insulation. The same system also influences brain development and the thickness of myelin later in life. The finding flips the script on stress—sometimes your body's stress response is exactly what you need to recover.
articles.takeaway: Stress hormones aren't always the enemy. When managed properly, they can mobilize your brain's repair systems after injury or stress.
articles.source: Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry / ScienceDaily

articles.headline: What You're Eating Could Be Quietly Raising Your Cancer Risk
articles.body: <cite index="47-2">In a nationally representative study of more than 17,000 U.S. men, those who ate more ultra-processed foods, including soft drinks, packaged snacks, cereals, and processed meats, had roughly 24% to 31% higher risks of prostate cancer after accounting for factors such as age, smoking, race and ethnicity, and poverty status.</cite> The study doesn't prove processed foods cause cancer, but the pattern is consistent across the data. Soft drinks, packaged snacks, and processed meats are the primary culprits. For busy professionals grabbing quick meals, this is worth paying attention to.
articles.takeaway: Cut back on soft drinks, packaged snacks, and processed meats. Real food swaps now could matter decades from now.
articles.source: Florida Atlantic University / American Journal of Medicine

articles.headline: Your Sweet Spot Is 6.4 to 7.8 Hours. Miss It and Your Body Ages Faster
articles.body: <cite index="19-1">The lowest levels of aging were seen among people who reported sleeping between 6.4 and 7.8 hours each day.</cite> Too little sleep and too much sleep both appear to accelerate aging at the cellular level. This isn't about willpower or habit hacks—it's biology. Your organs age faster when you're outside that narrow window. The research suggests duration matters more than perfection, so consistency beats random long sleeps.
articles.takeaway: Aim for the 6.5 to 7.5 hour range most nights. That's where your body actually slows aging.
articles.source: Columbia University Irving Medical Center / ScienceDaily

articles.headline: This Diet Cut Liver Fat by 67% in Just Months. Here's Why That Matters
articles.body: <cite index="57-1,57-2">All three groups lost about 10% of their body weight, but keto reduced liver fat by 67%, compared with 45% for the other diets. About half of the keto group also no longer qualified as having prediabetes after four to five months.</cite> Ketogenic, Mediterranean, and low-fat diets all worked for weight loss, but keto produced the strongest changes in liver health and blood sugar control. For people with fatty liver disease and prediabetes, the difference was dramatic.
articles.takeaway: If you have metabolic issues beyond weight, keto shows stronger metabolic improvements than other diets in the short term.
articles.source: Washington University School of Medicine / Cell Metabolism

workout.title: Press and Power: Chest and Shoulders in 30
workout.tip: Keep your core braced like you're about to take a punch on every pressing movement. If your lower back arches off the floor during floor presses, place your feet flat — it protects your spine and keeps tension where it belongs.
workout.warmup: Start with 30 seconds of arm circles (forward and backward), 10 shoulder rolls, and 10 slow push-up negatives — take 3 seconds to lower yourself down, then push back up normally. This primes your chest, shoulders, and triceps without fatiguing them.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.notes: Lie flat with knees bent. Press straight up, locking out at the top. Lower slowly — 2-3 seconds down. Full range of motion matters more than heavy weight.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press (Standing)
exercises.notes: Stand tall, core tight. Press dumbbells from shoulder height directly overhead. Avoid flaring your elbows out wide — keep them at roughly 45 degrees. Squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Push-Up to Alternating Shoulder Tap
exercises.notes: Do one push-up, then tap your right hand to your left shoulder while holding a plank. Alternate sides. Keep your hips square — resist the urge to rotate. Easier: drop to your knees for the push-up portion only.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.notes: Light weight here. Lead with your elbows, not your hands. Stop at shoulder height. Go slower — 2 seconds up, 2 seconds down. These burn. That's the point.

exercises.name: Tricep Push-Up (Close-Grip)
exercises.notes: Hands directly under your chest, elbows tracking back along your ribs — not flaring out. Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor. If full push-ups are too hard, elevate your hands on a couch or chair.

workout.cooldown: Finish with a 60-second doorframe chest stretch (arms on each side of a door frame, lean forward gently) and a 30-second overhead tricep stretch per arm. Breathe slowly. You earned it.

meal.title: Seared Trout and Farro Bowl with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes and Herb Yogurt
meal.description: Cook a big batch of farro at the start of the week and store it in the fridge. It reheats in 90 seconds and makes high-protein bowls like this a 15-minute weeknight dinner.
meal.instructions:
Ingredients:
2 trout fillets (about 5 oz each), skin on
1 cup cooked farro
1 cup cherry tomatoes
1 cup baby spinach
1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt
1 tbsp fresh dill, chopped
1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
1 clove garlic, minced
Juice of half a lemon
1 tbsp olive oil
Salt and black pepper to taste
Pinch of smoked paprika

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400F. Toss cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a small baking tray and roast for 12 to 15 minutes until blistered. 2. While tomatoes roast, mix Greek yogurt with dill, parsley, garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper to make the herb yogurt. Set aside. 3. Pat trout fillets dry and season with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear trout skin-side down for 3 to 4 minutes until the skin is crispy, then flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. 4. Build bowls with farro as the base, add a handful of spinach, top with the trout fillet and roasted tomatoes, and finish with a generous spoonful of herb yogurt.
